system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
Auxiliary aids and alternative accessible formats
diagnosis: Effective communication accommodation for a patient with a vision disability
mechanism: Federal disability-rights requirements call for communication with patients with vision disabilities to be as effective as communication with others. When necessary, covered health programs should provide appropriate auxiliary aids or services such as qualified readers, Braille, large print, or accessible electronic formats, with the choice guided by effective communication and the individual's needs.
vignette: A 63-year-old woman with severe visual impairment is being counseled about a new long-term medication. She independently manages her health decisions but cannot read the standard-print medication instructions. She asks for the information in an electronic format compatible with her screen reader.
lead: Which response by the clinic is most appropriate?
correct: Provide the instructions in an accessible electronic format that permits effective communication
distractors: Require a family member to read the standard-print instructions to her
Provide the standard-print instructions because the same document is given to all patients
Ask her to sign a waiver stating that written instructions cannot be provided
Withhold written information and rely only on a brief verbal summary
distractor_notes: A support person does not remove the covered entity's responsibility to ensure effective communication when an auxiliary aid or accessible format is needed.
Providing identical inaccessible material does not make communication equally effective for a patient with a vision disability.
The appropriate response is to furnish an effective auxiliary aid or accessible format rather than shift the accessibility burden to the patient.
The nature and complexity of the communication matter; an accessible format can provide the same information independently rather than unnecessarily limiting the patient to a shortened summary.
key_expl: HHS disability-rights rules require covered health programs to take appropriate steps to ensure communication with people with vision disabilities is as effective as communication with others. Auxiliary aids and services can include Braille, large print, qualified readers, and accessible electronic information usable with a screen reader.
objective: Apply disability-access principles by selecting an effective accessible format for a patient with visual impairment rather than relying on family members, inaccessible standard print, waivers, or reduced information.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Autosomal recessive pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1 due to epithelial sodium channel dysfunction
mechanism: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in SCNN1A, SCNN1B, or SCNN1G reduce epithelial sodium channel activity. Impaired distal sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion cause neonatal salt wasting with hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and dehydration; ENaC dysfunction outside the kidney can also produce pulmonary and skin manifestations.
vignette: A 2-month-old boy has recurrent episodes of severe dehydration. Laboratory studies repeatedly show hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. He has also had recurrent lower respiratory tract infections. Plasma aldosterone concentration is markedly elevated.
lead: Loss of function of which transport protein most directly explains this patient's disorder?
distractor_notes: ROMK loss can cause a Bartter phenotype with renal salt wasting, but the characteristic electrolyte disturbance includes hypokalemia rather than aldosterone-resistant hyperkalemia.
Loss of the thiazide-sensitive sodium-chloride cotransporter causes Gitelman syndrome, which produces renal salt wasting with hypokalemia rather than hyperkalemia.
Loss of the thick-ascending-limb Na-K-2Cl cotransporter causes Bartter syndrome and does not produce the systemic ENaC phenotype.
CFTR dysfunction causes cystic fibrosis, but it does not explain aldosterone-resistant hyperkalemic salt wasting from impaired distal sodium reabsorption.
key_expl: Autosomal recessive pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1 is caused by loss-of-function variants in ENaC subunits. Reduced ENaC activity decreases sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion despite high aldosterone, producing hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and dehydration; extra-renal ENaC dysfunction can cause recurrent pulmonary manifestations.
objective: Connect neonatal salt wasting, hyperkalemia, high aldosterone, and extra-renal manifestations to ENaC dysfunction in autosomal recessive pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease due to PLP1 dysfunction
mechanism: PLP1 variants disrupt proteolipid protein 1/DM20 production, folding, trafficking, or availability in oligodendrocyte membranes. Because these proteins are major components of central nervous system myelin, the result is hypomyelination and progressive neurologic dysfunction, usually in males with X-linked inheritance.
vignette: A 10-month-old boy has persistent nystagmus, delayed motor development, hypotonia, and progressive difficulty controlling head and trunk movements. Brain MRI shows diffuse hypomyelination. His maternal uncle had a similar childhood neurologic disorder.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractor_notes: Alexander disease is a GFAP-related leukodystrophy characterized by abnormal astroglial Rosenthal fibers rather than the classic X-linked PLP1 hypomyelination pattern.
Krabbe disease is caused by GALC deficiency with toxic galactolipid accumulation and demyelination, not PLP1-related hypomyelination.
Canavan disease results from aspartoacylase deficiency and N-acetylaspartate accumulation rather than an X-linked myelin structural-protein defect.
Metachromatic leukodystrophy is a lysosomal sulfatide-storage disorder rather than the PLP1-associated X-linked hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
key_expl: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease is an X-linked leukodystrophy caused by PLP1 variants. Proteolipid protein 1 and DM20 are major components of CNS myelin; abnormal production or trafficking leads to hypomyelination, nystagmus, motor delay, and progressive neurologic impairment in affected males.
objective: Recognize Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease from early nystagmus, motor delay, diffuse hypomyelination, and an X-linked family pattern.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 due to AGXT deficiency
mechanism: AGXT encodes alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase, a peroxisomal liver enzyme that converts glyoxylate to glycine. Loss of enzyme activity or mistargeting away from peroxisomes causes glyoxylate accumulation and conversion to oxalate, leading to recurrent calcium oxalate stones, nephrocalcinosis, kidney failure, and systemic oxalosis.
vignette: A 16-year-old boy has recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis and progressive nephrocalcinosis despite high fluid intake. His younger sister has similar findings. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in AGXT.
lead: The deficient enzyme normally functions primarily in which cellular compartment?
distractor_notes: Some AGXT variants can mistarget the enzyme to mitochondria, but normal alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase functions in peroxisomes.
Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases but are not the normal compartment for alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase.
The key glyoxylate-to-glycine reaction mediated by AGXT occurs in hepatic peroxisomes rather than the cytosol.
The rough endoplasmic reticulum is involved in synthesis and processing of secreted/membrane proteins, not the normal site of AGXT-mediated glyoxylate metabolism.
key_expl: Alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase is a peroxisomal liver enzyme. AGXT variants reduce activity or misdirect the enzyme, allowing glyoxylate to accumulate and be converted to oxalate, which forms calcium oxalate deposits and stones.
objective: Connect primary hyperoxaluria type 1 to deficiency of the peroxisomal enzyme alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum due to ABCC6 dysfunction
mechanism: Loss of functional ABCC6/MRP6 is associated with abnormal deposition of calcium and other minerals in elastic fibers of the skin, retina, and arterial walls. This produces characteristic skin changes, retinal disease with visual loss, and premature vascular disease.
vignette: A 31-year-old woman has gradually developed yellowish papules and loose, inelastic skin along the sides of her neck. Ophthalmologic examination shows angioid streaks with prior retinal bleeding. She also reports calf pain when walking several blocks. Her parents are unaffected.
lead: Which tissue abnormality most directly accounts for this multisystem disorder?
correct: Abnormal mineral deposition in elastic fibers
distractors: Defective type I collagen triple-helix formation
Autoantibody-mediated disruption of type VII collagen
Excess degradation of elastin by neutrophil elastase
distractor_notes: Type I collagen defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta phenotypes rather than the characteristic skin-retinal-arterial mineralization pattern.
Fibrillin-1 defects cause Marfan syndrome and do not produce the typical mineralization of elastic fibers seen in pseudoxanthoma elasticum.
Type VII collagen autoimmunity causes epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, a blistering disorder rather than this inherited multisystem mineralization disease.
Unopposed neutrophil elastase is central to alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency lung disease, not the ABCC6-related mineralization of skin, retinal, and vascular elastic fibers.
key_expl: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum is caused by ABCC6 variants and is characterized by abnormal calcium and mineral accumulation in elastic fibers. The affected tissues include skin, the eye/retina, and arterial walls, explaining the combined cutaneous, visual, and vascular findings.
objective: Recognize pseudoxanthoma elasticum and connect its skin, retinal, and vascular manifestations to abnormal mineralization of elastic fibers.
clues: yellow papules and lax neck skin
